newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Moscow mayor hits out at potential power rivals.
newsitem.headline: Moscow mayor hits out at potential power rivals.

text.p: Moscow Mayor Yuri Luzhkov, widely regarded as a likely presidential candidate, said he had no immediate ambitions to be Russia's head of state but criticised his potential rivals in an interview published on Tuesday.
Luzhkov, 60, told the Komsomolskaya Pravda newspaper it was wrong even to discuss who would succeed President Boris Yeltsin while he prepares to have heart surgery in the next two months.
"I tell you with full responsibility -- I have not prepared and am not preparing (a presidential bid). What the future will bring, I don't know, but today I do not want to (make a bid)," he said.
"I am in the president's team and will be with the president until the end."
Luzhkov, who portrays himself as a man of action rather than words, won a second term as Moscow's mayor with a landslide victory in an election last June.

Some Russian newspapers and commentators have suggested Luzhkov has started unofficial campaigning to become president, travelling to other regions in recent weeks to try to boost his support outside the capital.

His potential rivals are widely regarded as Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, security chief Alexander Lebed and Communist Party leader Gennady Zyuganov. Little love is lost between Luzhkov and Anatoly Chubais, head of the Kremlin administration.
In the interview, Luzhkov praised Chernomyrdin as a strong economic manager who was keen to do good for Russia, and said Chubais was a better administrator than his predecessors.
But he criticised them both and had harsh words for Lebed and Zyuganov. Of the four, only Lebed and Zyuganov have openly stated that they have presidential ambitions.
Luzhkov condemned a peace deal signed by Lebed for breakaway Chechnya and regretted the security chief's outspoken comments in what many political analysts call manoeuvring for power.
"In this situation, it is in principle wrong to hold conversations such as Lebed is having after already declaring he is a contender (for president)," Luzhkov said.
He said Zyuganov's moment had passed with his failure in the presidential election runoff in July, in which Yeltsin won a new four-year term, and said Chubais' actions were dangerous.
"He uses the fact that the president is ill and starts deciding matters and influencing the situation from a level which was always the president's personal prerogative," Luzhkov said.
He said Chernomyrdin had failed to achieve strategic goals and had too great a love for the power industry in which he made his name.
